questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests candidates on multi-cluster configuration distribution, CRD design, real-time propagation mechanisms, and tenant isolation in cloud-native environments.

## Key Concepts

- **Per-tenant feature flags via CRD**: Custom resource definition enabling declarative flag management per tenant
- **Central store and reconciliation loop**: Operator pattern synchronizing flag state across clusters
- **Real-time propagation**: Immediate flag updates without pod restarts or redeployments
- **Deterministic conflict resolution**: Predefined priority rules (e.g., tenant-level overrides cluster-level) ensuring consistent behavior
- **Auditability and rollback**: Immutable change log with timestamp, actor, and previous value tracking
- **Tenant isolation and RBAC**: Namespace-scoped resources with role-based access controls preventing cross-tenant interference

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantFeatureFlag
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-flags
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  flags:
    new-path: true
  version: v1
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle flag propagation latency in geographically distributed clusters?
- What conflict resolution strategy would you implement when dev and staging environments require different flag values for the same tenant?
- How do you ensure flags are validated before applying to production gateways?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical policy design at the intersection of CNF gateways, Kubernetes admission control, and SBOM-driven security. It requires translating per-tenant risk tolerances into enforceable constraints and verifying end-to-end behavior.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA integration for admission control
- Per-namespace configuration and binding
- SBOM-driven vulnerability data (CVSS) attached to images
- Rego-based enforcement logic and concise ConstraintTemplates
- End-to-end testing: apply templates, constraints, and verify allow/deny outcomes

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: CNFImageVuln
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfimagevuln
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFImageVuln
      scope: Cluster
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package cnfimagevuln
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      # image.vulns is a list of {cve, cvss}
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.kind == "Deployment";
        ns := input.review.object.metadata.namespace;
        threshold := data.namespaceThresholds[ns];
        some i;
        vul := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["image.vulns"];
        cvss := vul[i].cvss;
        cvss > threshold; msg := sprintf("CVSS %v exceeds threshold %v for namespace %s", [cvss, threshold, ns]);
      }
```
```yaml
# Constraint: Bind per-namespace threshold
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: CNFImageVuln
metadata:
  name: cnf-image-vuln-namespace
spec:
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - {key: "cnf.namespace", operator: In, values: ["default"]}
```
```yaml
# Test manifest: should fail for CVSS > threshold and pass otherwise
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-cnf
  namespace: default
  annotations:
    image.vulns: "[{\"cve\":\"CVE-2024-0001\",\"cvss\":9}]"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-cnf
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-cnf
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/cnf:latest
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle multi-tenant overrides for temporary risk surges?
- How would you test performance impact of SBOM parsing in high-scale deployments?
